reason: The text portrays Egypt's elite unfavorably through multiple elements: Pharaoh (the king) is depicted as obstinate, having his heart hardened and pursuing the Israelites; his military leadership and forces (chariots, horsemen, and army) are shown pursuing the Israelites into the sea and are completely destroyed—'not one of them remained' (לֹֽא־ נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּהֶ֖ם עַד־ אֶחָֽד). The passage emphasizes their role as enemies of God's people and their ultimate annihilation as a demonstration of God's power, which constitutes an unfavorable portrayal.
story: The Parting of the Red Sea
